content.title: Threat Relay Reversal | Rescue, Tool Transfer, and Renewed Defense
content.summary: A larger second-order threat removes the first threat but inherits pursuit of the same injured adult. The adult carries that physical state toward two rescuers; their first intervention only suppresses the threat long enough to expose a usable tool, and the protagonist joins collective defense before the larger threat visibly resumes.

quick_start.input_format: clearly adult injured protagonist, first-order threat and rescue direction established together + larger second-order threat removes the old threat and inherits the pursuit target + injury or exhaustion persists toward at least two adult rescuers + first intervention is only temporary and exposes one usable tool + protagonist acquires the tool and joins collective defense + larger threat resumes before the next impact
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult polar researcher limps toward two adult station guards after a translucent shelf predator captures a smaller ice burrower. Light cables drop the larger creature only briefly, exposing a grounding emitter; the researcher joins the defense line as the predator's internal cracks glow and its head rises again.
required_anchors: Establish one clearly adult vulnerable protagonist, a first-order threat and a visible rescue direction in one geography.
Let a larger second-order threat directly remove the first threat and immediately inherit pursuit of the same protagonist.
Make the rescuers' first intervention only temporarily suppress the larger threat while exposing one usable tool.
Let the protagonist acquire the tool and join collective defense before the larger threat resumes movement or re-enters.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A larger second-order threat removes the first threat but inherits pursuit of the same injured adult. The adult carries that physical state toward two rescuers; their first intervention only suppresses the threat long enough to expose a usable tool, and the protagonist joins collective defense before the larger threat visibly resumes.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult vulnerable protagonist, one first-order threat and a visible rescue direction inside a stable environment. Let a materially larger second-order threat enter the same geography and directly remove the first threat, but immediately inherit pursuit of the protagonist. Show the protagonist carrying a visible injury or exhaustion state toward at least two clearly adult rescuers; their first intervention creates only a temporary suppression and exposes one usable tool. The protagonist acquires that tool and joins the rescuers, then the second-order threat visibly resumes movement or re-enters before the end. The reusable mechanism is threat substitution, inherited pursuit, physically continuous escape, provisional rescue, tool acquisition and renewed collective defense—not the source survivor, creatures, forest, flame, weapons, uniforms, choreography, gore, watermark, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one clearly adult vulnerable protagonist, a first-order threat and a visible rescue direction in one geography.
invariants.purpose: Gives later threat substitution and escape a measurable baseline.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a rescue direction, each creature encounter reads as an unrelated insert.

invariants.rule: Let a larger second-order threat directly remove the first threat and immediately inherit pursuit of the same protagonist.
invariants.purpose: Turns apparent rescue into an escalation rather than a reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the larger threat ignores the protagonist, the danger chain ends instead of transferring.

invariants.rule: Carry one visible injury or exhaustion state through the protagonist's movement toward at least two adult rescuers.
invariants.purpose: Preserves the cost of the first conflict and makes rescue urgency legible.
invariants.ablation_failure: A fully reset sprint erases causal continuity.

invariants.rule: Make the rescuers' first intervention only temporarily suppress the larger threat while exposing one usable tool.
invariants.purpose: Creates a short reversal that enables the protagonist to change role.
invariants.ablation_failure: An instant permanent defeat leaves no reason for tool acquisition or cooperation.

invariants.rule: Let the protagonist acquire the tool and join collective defense before the larger threat resumes movement or re-enters.
invariants.purpose: Pays off the rescue as capability transfer while retaining threat escalation.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on the collapsed threat falsely resolves the core mechanism.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source adult survivor, face, body, clothing, injuries, expressions and exact performance
the source spider-like creature, larger forest monster, anatomy, attacks, mouth, limbs and gore
the source bioluminescent jungle, cyan plants, mud, roots, flame and exact lighting
the source soldiers, rifles, uniforms, shooting, crawling, combat choreography and camera path
the source creator identity, Topview challenge mark, Seedance 2.5 claim, watermark and 30-second timing
